builders.what_it_does:
P6 Stream diagnostic rows (joint order step 1). The rows ask one question: is the stream-only damage at 50% (CLIP 11.104, ResNet 18.051) a scale or mean problem, or lost content? All rows are stream-only cuts. They use the floor's stream order, computed on the input X (noisecut scores). Heads, MLP and inner channels stay at full width. The calculation uses no photos. Photos are for scoring only.

CLIP (one builder, _p6diag_clip.py; the modes differ only in the divisor of each norm):
| Rule | Divisor D_l at each of 26 sites (ln_pre, ln1/ln2 x 12, ln_post) |
|---|---|
| p6diag_clip_plain | baseline on X: vitgen.cut, LayerNorm over the kept dims (= split_stream, order from X) |
| p6diag_clip_k | rms form, D_l = k (the centring change alone) |
| p6diag_clip_D | rms form, D_l = 768 |
| p6diag_clip_rho | rms form, D_l = 768 * rho_l. rho_l = kept share of the centred stream energy at site l. Teacher on X, open loop. THE TEST ROW |
| p6diag_clip_grho | NULL: one global rho (the mean of the 26 rho_l) at every site |

How the stream is centred (SliceGPT form). J = I - 11^T/768 is folded into every writer (patch_w, cls, pos, o_w, o_b, pr_w, pr_b). Each norm's gain and bias are folded into its readers (q/k/v/fc weights and biases, and ln_post into proj). Every norm then becomes rms with g = 1 and b = 0. The ln_pre output is not centred, because J diag(g_pre) J is a full matrix. So the student keeps the floor's coordinates E of the centred stream, in a basis rotated inside the kept subspace: z = U^T E^T J x, from the SVD E^T J diag(g_pre) J = U S V^T. The rotation does not change which dims are kept, and the rms norms are rotation invariant. The student's ln_pre reads V^T J t with gain S. This is exact at f = 1. The ln_post bias keeps the floor's kept-dims share (b_post[kept] @ proj[kept]), exactly. No best-fit bias is used. The fold algebra runs in float64 on the CPU.
Prints for each f: rho_l at every site, and the realized divisor ratio at every site. The ratio is teacher divisor / student divisor, median over tokens, on the first 32 images of X, closed loop. A value of 1.00 means the student reads at the teacher's scale.

ResNet (one builder, _p6diag_r18.py). The cut is the same as _split.py: every read of a cut stream channel is set to 0.
| Rule | Fold |
|---|---|
| p6diag_r18_plain | none (baseline on X, = split_stream with the order from X) |
| p6diag_r18_meanfold | for each reader, c_r = the mean over images and positions of conv_r applied only to the cut channels, on the teacher stream on X. The zero-padded borders are included. Conv readers: bn.running_mean -= c_r (an edit of the inference map, never read as a statistic). fc: bias += c_r |
| p6diag_r18_permmean | NULL: the same computation with the cut channels' activations permuted among the cut channels of the stage (a derangement, seed = stage) |
Readers: stage s block-1 conv1, stage s+1 block-0 conv1 and downsample, stage-1 block-0 conv1 (stem), and fc. Each reader uses the mean of the stream point it reads. Prints: the mean of the cut channels against the kept channels per stage, and an in-rule CHECK. The CHECK passes by algebra: the max absolute difference between the folded reader's output mean and the teacher reader's output mean on X.

Implementation checks: at f = 1 every CLIP rms mode must give the teacher, because the conversion is exact. The ResNet check at f = 1 is vacuous, because nothing is cut. The ResNet fold evidence is the CHECK line at f < 1. Syntax: py_compile passes on all 10 files. Torch was not run.

builders.open_risks:
1. Nothing ran. The CLIP f=1 rows are the only test of the rms conversion. If the rho f=1 row gives KL >= 1e-3, stop all CLIP rows. The early-site realized-ratio print is the only CLIP check at f < 1.
2. The k row differs from plain in two things, not one. It centres over all 768 dims (teacher centring), and the ln_pre normalizer reads the subspace V^T J t, not the coordinates t[kept]. All rms rows share both changes.
3. rho_l is open loop. It is measured on the teacher's stream on X, not on the student's own stream. The realized-ratio print is closed loop, so at late sites it mixes stream drift with scale. Read the early sites for scale.
4. The ln_post bias keeps only the kept-dims share (as the floor does). It needs a nonzero ln_post gain on every kept dim, and an assert stops the build if one is zero.
5. ResNet: the fold uses teacher-stream means on pink X. F2 shows pink is off the operating point (variance ratio .12 in stage 4), so these means may also be off. The photo-mean check row is NOT built, because rules may not import a photo loader. The runner must build it as a separate check script if it is wanted.
6. ResNet f=1 rows are vacuous. The CHECK line at f < 1 passes by algebra (conv linearity plus the BN edit). It catches a sign or target error only. It is not evidence for the hypothesis.
7. The ResNet params column reports the full network, as in split_stream (masked weights stay in the tensors).
8. Memory: the CLIP helper keeps one teacher copy on MPS for each process (about 350 MB), and the r18 helper makes up to two model copies. Both are small, but the runner must check swap first.
9. Run time estimate: about 10-11 minutes in total (CLIP about 35 s for each f=1 check and 60-90 s for each 4-f row, ResNet under 30 s for each command).

builders.what_it_does:
I built three new scripts for P0 Input. I edited no harness file and no file of another builder. All three pass py_compile. I ran no torch.

1. make_input.py makes the self-made input and the null input for one network.
- It starts from the shared pink file, cache/input_pink_n256_s1.pt.
- The image is set in Fourier space with a 1/f amplitude. g(z) = chan_norm(irfft2(A*z, ortho)).
- x(z) = x0 + (g(z) - g(z0)). With K = 0, the output is the shared file bit for bit. This passes by algebra. The --k0-check flag also tests it with torch.equal and loads no network.
- Fixed knobs: N 256, K 32, Adam lr .05, batch 32, seed 1. The random transform does a roll of up to 16 px, a flip per image with p .5, and a zoom of .9-1.1 with a crop or a zero pad.
- ResNet loss: cross-entropy to a class y drawn from softmax(fc.bias), generator seed 1.
- CLIP loss: a self-InfoNCE proxy at scale 100. It compares each image with the previous step's detached embeddings. The negatives are the other images in the batch. This is not CLIP's training loss.
- The null uses the same recipe, with a shuffle inside every linear and conv weight tensor (shuffle seed 2). Norms, biases, cls and pos stay as they are. The images are made by the shuffled network.
- Output: cache/{net}_{self|null}_n256_k32_s1.pt as float16, plus a .json sidecar file. The sidecar holds the losses at step 1 and step K, how far each batch moved, the drift of the channel std, and (ResNet only) how often the network picks the drawn class.
- --smoke runs 1 batch for 2 steps and writes no file. It prints the time per step. With --kind null it also checks the shuffle (passes by algebra).
- The Fourier transform and the image transforms run on the CPU. Only the network runs on MPS. --render-dev mps moves them to MPS.
- Before it writes a file, the script stops if any value is not finite. It refuses to overwrite a file unless you give --force.

2. check_input.py runs the checks on any list of input files and on 1,000 held photos (reading only).
- ResNet: it imports check_bn.stats and check_bn.spearman. Per BN layer, it gives var rank, mean rank and var ratio against the stored running stats. It also gives medians for each stage (stem, layer1-4).
- ResNet firing rate: one hook on each block's bn1 output, in the same forward pass. It measures P(out > 0) per inner channel. Per block, it gives the Spearman against the photo rates and the median rate ratio.
- ResNet guards: the layer4 var ratio is above 2, or the fraction of channels with rate above .9 is more than 2x the photo fraction.
- CLIP: a copy of the noisecut.vit_scores loop, with the same formulas. It gives the Spearman of the floor's unit scores against the same scores on 1,000 held photos: stream (768), heads per block (12) and MLP per block (3,072). score_rank_median = the median of three numbers: the stream Spearman, the median head Spearman and the median MLP Spearman.
- CLIP extra readouts: the MLP firing rate of fc(ln2(x)), the RMS ratio of loud dims 163, 419, 171, 573 and 97 at each of 13 sites, and the top-10 eigenvalue share of the stream covariance at each site.
- CLIP guards: the top-1% score share (MLP and stream) is more than 2x the photo share, or the fraction of MLP units with rate above .9 is more than 2x the photo fraction.
- Implementation check (passes by algebra): on the first input, the copied loop must match noisecut.vit_scores with a relative error below 1e-4.
- An assert checks that the stored logit scale is 100.
- --extra MODULE:FUNC is a hook for P5's score(W, X).
- Output: check_input.json, merged per input name.

3. check_mix.py is the mandatory planted test. It is labelled as a reading check.
- Inputs: 4 mixes of 256 images with 0, 25, 50 and 100% held photos. The photos are the second held photo of 256 classes spread over the 1,000, in a fixed shuffled order. They are different from the 1,000 reference photos. The rest of each mix is the shared pink images.
- The pass rules were fixed before any run:
  (1) Each gating score rises strictly with the mix. The gating scores are the three readouts the proposal names: ResNet var rank median, ResNet firing-rate Spearman median, and CLIP score-rank median. The other scores are printed only.
  (2) The ResNet var rank at 100% minus the var rank at 0% is .40 or more.
  (3) The floor built on the 50% mix, ResNet f = .05, gives a KL on 1,000 test photos that is more than 7.541 and less than 14.949.
- Implementation check: mix000 is the pink file.
- Rule 3 calls noisecut.r18 and board.r18_score directly. It writes nothing to board.json or cache/.
- Output: check_mix.json.

Knob choice I fixed myself: the scale of z. The proposal did not state it. z0 is scaled to RMS 1 per image and channel (a unit white seed in an orthonormal Fourier basis), so Adam's lr of .05 is a real step size. With torch's default FFT scale, the images would move by less than 1%. The docstring records this choice, and nothing may retune it.

Predictions are copied from the proposal without change. Only the ResNet floor baselines changed, to the shared-file floor: 1.665 / 9.386 / 14.949.

builders.what_it_does:
P5 Rank is built. No torch run happened. Only py_compile ran, and every file passed it.

rules/p5rank.py gives vit(T, f, X=None) and r18(A, f, X=None).
1. Every unit has a mask per input. The score of a unit is S_u = mean over inputs of (dJ_n/dm_u)^2. dJ/dm is the written value times the read gradient, summed over tokens.
2. The probe is the one in the proposal. CLIP: J = r . 100e/||e||, r ~ N(0, I). ResNet: J = r . logits, r is a centred Gaussian. Each input has one seeded r, so every step uses the same r.
3. Greedy schedule: 1, .95, .85, .75, .65, .5, .4, .3, .25, .18, .12, .08, .05. At each step the rule scores the kept units on the masked network. Then it removes the lowest units in each set (stream, head per block, MLP per block; ResNet stream per stage, inner per block). Sizes come from vitgen.sizes and wide18.widths.
4. Each unit keeps its removal step and its score at removal. Keep(k) = the k units removed last. One nested order gives every size.
5. The build is a plain cut: vitgen.cut or wide18.cut_from_a. No weight changes.
6. The CLIP stream mask is masked at ln_pre, ln1, ln2 and ln_post (the critic's fix). The divisor is the kept count. Heads are masked before o_w. MLP neurons are masked at the GELU output.
7. ResNet: inner channels are masked after relu(bn1). Stream channels are masked at every read. The forward is written by hand with non-inplace ReLU. The rule uses a private copy of A with no parameter gradients.
8. Cache file: fanout/cache/p5rank_{net}_{input hash}_s{seed}[_null][_to.5]_v1.pt. Every size and every split rule uses the same cache.
9. A per-step readout of the probe error (no photos) is saved for all parts cut and for each part alone. CLIP uses 32 inputs for it.
10. API for other parts: order, keep, rank, score.

Other rules:

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| p5rank_null | Same formula, with a fixed single-cycle permutation of the read pairing inside each set: G_null = sum_t a[u] g[pi(u)]. The CLIP null order stops at f = .5. |
| p5rank_mlp, p5rank_heads, p5rank_stream (both nets), p5rank_inner (ResNet) | Cut one set by the P5 order. The other sets stay at full width. ResNet sets are zeroed as in _split. |
| p5rank_null_mlp, p5rank_null_heads | The same one-set cuts, with the null order. |
| magsplit_mlp, magsplit_heads | The weight-ranking fail line: magcut scores, one set cut, weights only. |
| p5rank1 | One-shot cut from the step-1 scores. |
| p5rank_s2 | Probe seed 2, for the seed spread. |

p5check.py runs these steps in this order:
1. Smoke: a 2-step greedy on 32 inputs, not saved. It runs every builder, the null and the one-set cuts, and it checks nesting.
2. I1: the masked forward equals the cut, in CPU float64 at f = 1, .95 and .5. The pass line is KL < 1e-5. CLIP uses a proxy KL with a random class matrix (no photos).
3. I2: the null hooks with the identity pairing must equal dJ/dm.
4. T1 (CLIP): a neuron with pr_w = 0 must score exactly 0. T2 (ResNet): the score must not change under a ReLU rescale.
5. If any check fails, the script stops with exit 1 and builds no cache.
6. If all checks pass, it builds the real order. Then it runs T3 (the planted test that can fail) on CLIP, T2 on ResNet, and prints the readout.

I1, I2, T1 and T2 are implementation checks. They pass by algebra. T3 is the planted test.

builders.what_it_does:
P4 Write rule, round 1. The stream fold is off (A = 0). The stream is cut as in the floor.

How it works:
1. The kept sets are the floor's sets: noisecut scores on the same input X.
2. The student is built front to back, one writer site at a time. CLIP sites are o_w and pr_w in each block. ResNet sites are conv2 in each block.
3. At each site, the code runs the teacher on its own stream. It runs the student on the student's own stream. Both use the generic input X.
4. It collects two moments in float64 on the CPU. S_x = E[a a'^T] uses the teacher's firings (all units) and the student's firings (kept units). S_s = E[a' a'^T] uses the student's firings only.
5. It solves one closed form: W' = W G, with G = (S_x + lam E_K)(S_s + lam I)^-1. Write biases stay the same.
6. lam = tr(S_s) / N_samples. N_samples is read from the firing tensor. Nothing is tuned.
7. The ResNet rule applies G to every 3x3 tap of conv2: einsum('onhw,nk->okhw').
8. The reader metric M cancels from G. So the M = I check is NOT APPLICABLE with A = 0.

Why the ridge pulls toward the plain slice (E_K) and not toward 0:
- With the slice anchor, the proposal's own stated identities hold. With a' = a_K it gives W_K + W_C P. At f = 1 it gives W. With no upstream change, closed loop equals open loop.
- The proposal's literal form, W S_x (S_s + lam)^-1, also shrinks the kept writes. That makes the output less sure: the critic's calibration confound.
- The literal form is kept as the switch anchor="zero".

Variants (all in rules/):
- p4write: whole network. CLIP cuts stream + heads + MLP. ResNet cuts stream + inner.
- p4write_mlp and p4write_heads (CLIP), p4write_inner (ResNet): one set cut and folded. The other sets keep full width and teacher weights.
- p4write_null, p4write_null_mlp, p4write_null_heads, p4write_null_inner: the shuffled-pairing null. The cut units' teacher firings come from the next image, at the same positions. The kept-to-kept pairing stays true. In expectation this is the mean-only fold per position, so it is also the calibration control.
- p4write_off_mlp, p4write_off_heads, p4write_off_inner: the plain slice (fold off) through the same code, on the same X. p4write_off_inner is the floor to compare p4write_inner against. The board's split_inner used a different pink draw.

Readouts: each build saves out/p4write_<tag>_f<f>_n256.json and prints one line. Per site, they hold lam, k, n, and the message residual on X for the floor and for the rule. For CLIP, they also hold sigma'/sigma at every LN site, for the rule and for the floor.

Built-in assert (passes by algebra): at every folded site, the rule's residual on X must be at or below the floor's residual. This catches a transposed G or a wrong index map.

p4write_check.py, run on the first 16 images of X:
- K1: synthetic fold. An exact copy at lam = 0 gives P = 1. The kept rows of G stay I.
- K2 and K5: every variant builds, the residual assert passes, and the output is finite.
- K3 and K6: at f = 1, the rule equals the teacher.
- K4 and K7: closed loop equals open loop at the first site, where nothing upstream changed.
All of these pass by algebra. They test the code only. The nulls carry the evidence.

Photo use: none in the calculation. Photos are for scoring only (board.py).
